LESSON: THE CELL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science 1.1 Introduction to General Science (8 lessons) ● Importance of Gen
Topic 1.2: The Cell
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Cell, part of Life Science 1.1 Introduction to General Science (8 lessons) ● Importance of Gen in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is the cell a basic unit of life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Cell together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner constructs a model of plant and animal cells as seen under the electron

microscope.

● Digital literacy: as the learner searches for information from the internet using devices with assistive technology on the

structure of a cell.

● Learning to learn: as the learner carries out the project work, reflects and adjusts appropriately.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinion while working on practical activities in groups such as construction of

models.

● Social justice: as the learner seeks equity, equality and gender consideration in distribution of learning resources such as

sharing of materials for making cell models.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Environmental conservation; as the learner manages wastes responsibly to

avoid pollution while preparing plant and animal cell models.

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Safety and security; as the learner observes safety precautions when

preparing the models.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Light microscope,

• Print media with appropriate colour contrast and font,

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers or screen magnifiers,

• Print textbooks in appropriate font and color,

• Braille textbooks.

7

Key Skills:

● Constructing a concept map of the levels of cell organisation, (for learners with low vision) or

● Interpret tactile map of the levels of cell organisation, (for learners with blindness)
